newsitem.title: UK: Profit takers move in on European bourses.
newsitem.headline: Profit takers move in on European bourses.

text.p: Profit-takers moved in on most leading European stock markets on Monday, using interest rate jitters and a weaker Wall Street as an excuse to take a breather after last week's records.
German shares were the notable exception, with the DAX index climbing to record highs again on buying prompted more by the futures market than by any enthusiasm among physical investors.
The dollar also paused after its recent surge, although it was firmer than late Friday levels in Europe, as dealers awaited purchasing data from the United States later in the day.

London and Paris were the main hunting grounds for investors seeking profits after both markets closed at record highs on Friday. However, both also recovered some of their early losses over the morning.
London's FTSE-100 index was down 13 points at 4,262.8 by the early afternoon while in Paris, the CAC-40 was off 5.76 at 2,510.80.
Worries about whether interest rates will rise this week made investors tred carefully.
"This is very much a defensive mark down," said one London dealer. "Volumes are very small."

Few people wanted to get involved in the market until monetary meetings on both sides of the Atlantic this week were over. "I think (a rate hike) is unlikely in the U.S., but we could still see one here," the London dealer said.
In the United States, the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FMOC) starts a two-day meeting on Tuesday while British monetary authorities are scheduled to meet on Wednesday.
Despite the signs that the United States is achieving inflation-free growth, Tuesday is the third anniversary of an unexpected U.S. interest rate hike which sent world stock markets plunging.
Wall Street also affected sentiment as its rally faltered on Friday and the Dow Jones industrial average ended 10.77 points lower at 6,813.09, although most broader indices held on to gains.
The exception was Germany, where the DAX index headed further into record territory and was up 24.46 points at 3,059.61.
But Frankfurt dealers said the rise was technical, driven by futures players, and they expressed the same interest rate concerns as their counterparts elsewhere in Europe.
The dollar was quiet as dealers awaited indications on the U.S. economy from the latest survey from the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM), due at 1500 GMT.
Dealers were also keeping an eye on a meeting of deputy finance ministers from the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations in Frankfurt.
The deputy ministers are preparing the agenda for a meeting of G7 finance ministers and central bank governors at the weekend.
The dollar was at 1.6473 marks and 122.08 yen at early afternoon, generally stable but up from 1.6365 marks and 121.12 yen in late European trade on Friday.
A report from the European statistics agency Eurostat, which assessed accounting practices European Union governments have used to meet the criteria for monetary union (EMU), had little effect.
It said that central bank gold sales could not be used for cutting deficits to meet criteria laid down in the Maastricht treaty.
CURRENCIES AT 1220 GMT
The dollar was at 1.6473 marks and 122.08 yen, up from 1.6365 marks and 121.12 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1220 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 13.0 points at 4,262.8.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 24.46 points at a record high of 3,059.61.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 5.76 at 2,510.80.
PRECIOUS METALS - Gold was at $344.35 an ounce after being fixed at $343.75 and against $345.50 previously. Silver was at $4.9, down two cents.
